r1_s1.text: Sunday morning. The pancakes are a little burnt, the kids are laughing, and he is humming off-key. It feels easy.

choices.recap: soaked it in
choices.label: Soak it in

choices.recap: noticed the unopened bills by the door
choices.label: Notice the unopened bills by the door

r1_s2a.text: He pulls you into a hug and the kids pile on. Later, almost in passing, he says work has been slow.

choices.recap: asked how he really feels
choices.label: Ask how he really feels

choices.recap: let it go because it was Sunday
choices.label: Let it go. It’s Sunday.

choices.recap: wondered when they stopped wanting the same things
choices.label: Wonder when the two of you stopped wanting the same things

choices.recap: noticed he had started asking where they were
choices.label: Notice he has started asking where you were

r1_s2b.text: You open one envelope. The number is bigger than you expected, and he sees your face.

choices.recap: showed him
choices.label: Show him

choices.recap: hid it for now
choices.label: Hide it for now

choices.recap: let him take over the bills
choices.label: Let him take over the bills

r1_s3a.text: He tells you the slow months have really been three months. He says it like a confession, then waits to see how you will take it.

choices.recap: said they would manage it together
choices.label: “We’ll manage it together.”

choices.recap: asked why he hadn’t said sooner
choices.label: “Why didn’t you tell me sooner?”

choices.recap: noticed how differently they take bad news
choices.label: Notice how differently the two of you take bad news

r1_s3b.text: That evening his mother calls during dinner. “Are you two managing?” she asks him, not you. He answers for both of you.

choices.recap: took the phone and spoke for themselves
choices.label: Take the phone and speak for yourself

choices.recap: let him handle it
choices.label: Let him handle it

choices.recap: told him to handle the money, then
choices.label: “Fine. You handle the money, then.”

choices.recap: realised they have never once agreed on how to handle anything
choices.label: Realise you have never once agreed on how to handle anything

r1_s4a.text: His shoulders drop. The kids have drawn on the fridge door again, and for a moment you both laugh at nothing.

choices.recap: sat down tonight and made a plan
choices.label: Sit down tonight and make a plan

choices.recap: said it can wait until the weekend
choices.label: Say it can wait until the weekend

choices.recap: said the money wasn’t the real problem
choices.label: “Honestly? The money isn’t the real problem.”

r1_s4b.text: “I was handling it,” he says. The word hangs in the air between you.

choices.recap: said partners don’t do it alone
choices.label: “We're partners, you shouldn't be handling it alone.”

choices.recap: dropped it
choices.label: Drop it. Not today.

choices.recap: asked “With what money?”
choices.label: “Handling it? With what money?”

choices.recap: said it wasn’t only about money
choices.label: “I don’t think this is only about the money.”

r1_s4c.text: Rain starts against the window. He ends the call and says nothing about what his mother said.

choices.recap: asked what she said
choices.label: Ask what she said

choices.recap: turned the television up
choices.label: Turn the television up

choices.recap: said what they have both been avoiding
choices.label: Say what you have both been avoiding

r1_end_open.text: You go through it together at the kitchen table. It isn’t fun, but neither of you is facing it alone.

r1_end_quiet.text: The day stays warm. The talk about money is folded up and put away, like a letter you mean to answer later. Something small has been saved for another day.

r1_end_strain.text: You go to bed with the dishes half done and your backs to each other. It is a small thing, the first of its kind, and you both notice.

r1_c1.text: He takes over the money kindly, and without a fuss. Within a day your bank card is in his wallet. “Easier this way,” he says, smiling. “You don’t need to worry about any of it.”

choices.recap: let him take over
choices.label: Let him. It does feel easier.

choices.recap: asked for their card back
choices.label: Ask for your card back

choices.recap: started putting cash aside in secret
choices.label: Say nothing, but start putting cash aside

r1_c2a.text: A few weeks on, you ask for money for your sister’s birthday gift. He asks what it is for, then how much, then why so much. He gives you half. The receipt is expected.

choices.recap: handed him the receipt without a word
choices.label: Hand him the receipt without a word

choices.recap: refused to show a receipt
choices.label: “I’m an adult. I don’t need to show a receipt.”

r1_c2b.text: He laughs, lightly, but his hand closes over yours on the wallet. “Why? Don’t you trust me?” The smile does not move.

choices.recap: backed down
choices.label: Back down: “No, it’s fine.”

choices.recap: demanded the card back
choices.label: “It’s mine. Give it back.”

choices.recap: suggested a joint account
choices.label: Suggest a joint account you can both see

r1_c2c.text: The notes are in a tea tin behind the rice. Your hands are shaking as you count them, and you hate that they are. Something small has quietly become a secret.

choices.recap: told him about it tonight
choices.label: Tell him about it tonight

choices.recap: kept it hidden, just in case
choices.label: Keep it hidden, just in case

r1_c3a.text: The rules multiply so quietly they never feel like rules. Who you text. How long you stay at your sister’s. He checks your phone “because he worries.” Your sister stops calling. She says you always seem busy.

textIf.add: He already knows where you are. He asks anyway.

choices.recap: called their sister anyway, from the stairwell
choices.label: Call your sister anyway, from the stairwell

choices.recap: handed over their phone unasked
choices.label: Hand him the phone before he asks

choices.recap: called it control out loud
choices.label: Say it out loud: “This isn’t worry. This is control.”

choices.recap: stopped answering their sister
choices.label: Stop picking up your sister’s calls, to avoid the questions

r1_c3b.text: He doesn’t shout. He goes quiet, which is worse. Dinner goes cold. By morning the card is back on the counter, next to a list of everything he has “done for you.”

choices.recap: took the card and said thank you
choices.label: Take the card and say thank you

choices.recap: said they would talk about it tonight
choices.label: Take the card and the list: “We’re talking about this tonight.”

r1_c3c.text: He listens with his arms folded. “A joint account,” he repeats, as if tasting the words. “Fine. Let’s do that.” You cannot tell whether you have won something or been handled.

choices.recap: went to the bank together tomorrow
choices.label: Go to the bank together tomorrow

choices.recap: waited to see if he followed through
choices.label: Wait and see whether he follows through

r1_c4a.text: Your sister picks up on the first ring. “Are you okay?” Your throat closes. You have rehearsed a hundred excuses and none of them come out. Above you, a door opens. “Who are you talking to?”

choices.recap: hung up on their sister
choices.label: “Nobody. I’ll call you back.”

choices.recap: whispered for their sister to come
choices.label: Whisper: “I need you to come and get me.”

r1_c4b.text: You stop mentioning your friends. You stop buying things. Then one night you realise you have not made a single decision all week, and nobody forced you. You simply stopped.

choices.recap: asked for space of their own
choices.label: Tell him you need some space of your own

choices.recap: let it be
choices.label: Let it be. It’s quieter this way.

choices.recap: booked a visit to their sister’s, no explanation
choices.label: Book a visit to your sister’s, no explanation

r1_c4c.text: He sets his glass down very carefully. “Control?” For a moment his face belongs to a stranger. Then his hand closes around your wrist. Not hard, he will say later. Barely anything. He holds it there.

choices.recap: froze and didn’t pull away
choices.label: Don’t pull away. Don’t breathe.

choices.recap: told him to let go
choices.label: “Let go of my wrist.”

choices.recap: pulled free and stepped back
choices.label: Pull free and step back

r1_c5a.text: He lets go and smiles as if nothing happened. “You’re being dramatic.” The marks will fade by morning. What you were about to say will take longer.

choices.recap: photographed their wrist
choices.label: Photograph your wrist when he is asleep

choices.recap: agreed they were being dramatic
choices.label: Agree: “Maybe I was.”

r1_c5b.text: He lets go at once and steps back, palms open, as if you were the one who grabbed. Then his eyes go to the keys on the hook, and back to you. “Where do you think you’re going?”

choices.recap: took the keys and walked out
choices.label: Take the keys and walk out

choices.recap: stayed to calm him down
choices.label: Stay. Try to calm him down.

r1_end_repair.text: It is a small thing: two names on one account. But it is the first time in months that a decision about your life was made by both of you.

r1_end_sister.text: She doesn’t ask for details. She says, “I’m coming on Saturday.” For the first time in weeks, someone outside this house knows.

r1_end_smaller.text: Nothing dramatic happens. That is what people will not understand later. The world just gets smaller, one reasonable-sounding rule at a time, until it is exactly the size of this house.

r1_end_proof.text: You photograph the faint marks with a hand that will not stay still, and hide the picture where he won’t look. It is not a plan yet. It is the first thing that is only yours.

r1_end_out.text: The keys are cold in your hand. You are on the stairs before you hear anything behind you. You do not know where you are going yet. You only know it is not back.

r1_end_grip.text: “Don’t you walk away from me.” The keys leave your hand. The hallway light clicks off. Whatever happens next will not be small.

r1_m1.text: It was never really the bills. You both know it. For months you have run the house like colleagues, and tonight, at the kitchen table, there is nobody left to perform for.

choices.recap: said they weren’t happy
choices.label: Say it: “I don’t think we are happy.”

choices.recap: asked whether he has felt it too
choices.label: Ask whether he has felt it too

choices.recap: lost their nerve and went back to the bills
choices.label: Lose your nerve and go back to the bills

r1_m2a.text: He doesn’t flinch. He looks almost relieved, which is the strangest part. “No,” he says. “I haven’t been either.”

choices.recap: asked if he wanted to try again
choices.label: “Do you want to try again?”

choices.recap: asked “Then what are we doing?”
choices.label: “Then what are we doing?”

r1_m2b.text: He puts the pen down. “Since the spring,” he says. “I just didn’t know how to say it without making it your fault.”

choices.recap: said it wasn’t his fault either
choices.label: “It isn’t your fault either.”

choices.recap: asked why he said nothing
choices.label: “Why did you say nothing?”

r1_m3a.text: You try, properly. Counselling on Tuesdays, a weekend away, a rota for the children. It is kind, and it is exhausting. One evening the counsellor asks what each of you wants. You answer at the same moment, and it is the same answer.

choices.recap: said “Not this” together
choices.label: Say it together: “Not this.”

choices.recap: asked for three more months
choices.label: Ask for three more months

r1_m3b.text: You talk until the kettle has gone cold twice. Nobody is guilty. He says, “I don’t want us to turn into people who can’t stand each other.” You find that you don’t want that either.

choices.recap: said “Let’s do this properly”
choices.label: “Then let’s do this properly.”

choices.recap: decided not to decide tonight
choices.label: “Let’s not decide tonight.”

r1_m4.text: Practical questions arrive faster than feelings. Who tells the children, and how. Who keeps the flat. He writes a list, and you add to it. It is oddly gentle work.

choices.recap: told the children together, and kept it simple
choices.label: Tell the children together, and keep it simple

choices.recap: asked a mediator to help with the rest
choices.label: Ask a mediator to help with the rest

choices.recap: asked for a week before signing
choices.label: Say you need a week before anything is signed

r1_end_conv.text: You sit on the sofa with the children between you and say it plainly: you both love them, and you are both staying their parents. It hurts. It is also true, and they can tell.

r1_end_mediated.text: The mediator’s office smells of coffee and printer ink. Nobody raises their voice. By the end of the hour you have agreed on more than you expected, and grieved more than you planned to.

r1_end_months.text: You agree to wait, and you both know what you are waiting for. It isn’t anger. It is the quiet of two people who have already said the hard part.

r1_p1.text: It was never one big fight. It is the small things done differently: he plans the week on Sunday night, and you find out your week on Monday morning. He likes a quiet house and you like a full one. For years you called it charming. Lately you have noticed that you stopped.

choices.recap: teased him about his colour-coded calendar
choices.label: Tease him about his colour-coded calendar

choices.recap: asked if they had become different people
choices.label: Ask: “Do you ever feel like we are different people?”

choices.recap: kept the peace and said nothing
choices.label: Keep the peace and say nothing

r1_p2a.text: He laughs, and then he doesn’t. “You always say it like it’s a joke,” he says. “It doesn’t always feel like one.” One of the children looks up from the table.

choices.recap: asked what he means
choices.label: Ask what he means

choices.recap: changed the subject
choices.label: Change the subject

r1_p2b.text: He takes his time. “Yes,” he says at last. “But I used to like that about you.” The kettle clicks off behind you, and neither of you moves.

choices.recap: asked what changed
choices.label: “I used to like it about you too. What changed?”

choices.recap: said maybe they like different things now
choices.label: “Maybe we like different things now.”

r1_p2c.text: Weeks of small concessions follow. You go to his sister’s dinner instead of the concert. He skips the party he was looking forward to. Each time, someone says “No problem” a little too quickly.

choices.recap: kept a quiet tally of what they have given up
choices.label: Keep a quiet tally of what you have given up

choices.recap: suggested taking turns
choices.label: Suggest taking turns: one weekend his, one weekend yours

r1_p3a.text: You sit down at the kitchen table and write the rule on the back of an envelope: one weekend his idea, the next weekend yours. It is oddly easy. It is also a little sad that it needed a rule.

choices.recap: tried it for three months and saw
choices.label: Try it for three months and see

choices.recap: added one evening a week with nothing planned at all
choices.label: Add one evening a week with nothing planned at all

r1_p3b.text: The tally grows longer than either of you admits. At a friend’s barbecue he gently corrects a story you are telling, in front of everyone. Nobody else notices. You do.

choices.recap: asked him not to correct them in public
choices.label: “Please don’t correct me in front of people.”

choices.recap: laughed it off and added it to the list
choices.label: Laugh it off and add it to the list

r1_p3c.text: He nods slowly. “So what do we do with that?” It is not an accusation. It is a real question, and neither of you has an answer ready.

choices.recap: looked for what they still share
choices.label: “Maybe we look for what we still share.”

choices.recap: said they don’t have to share everything
choices.label: “Maybe we don’t have to share everything.”

choices.recap: admitted they didn’t know
choices.label: “I honestly don’t know.”

r1_p4.text: Years of small differences line up, and for the first time you see them as one thing. It is not a quarrel. It is a direction. He wants a life that is quiet and planned, and you want one that is open. Neither of you is wrong, and you cannot both have it.

choices.recap: said they wanted different lives
choices.label: Say it plainly: “I think we want different lives.”

choices.recap: asked for time before deciding anything
choices.label: Ask for time before deciding anything

choices.recap: suggested counselling, to learn each other’s language
choices.label: Suggest counselling, to learn each other’s language

r1_end_turns.text: Three months later the envelope is still on the fridge, soft at the corners. Some weekends are his and some are yours. It is not a perfect system, but you both know the rules, and you have stopped keeping score.

r1_end_translate.text: You will never want the same things. You are starting to understand that this is not the problem. It is the work. He explains his calendar, and you explain your Mondays, and it is the most honest talk you have had in years.

r1_end_tally.text: Nothing is wrong enough to say out loud, and nothing is right enough to let go of. The list grows quietly in both your heads. You are still here, and you are both still counting.

r1_end_different.text: He doesn’t argue. He says, “I think I knew,” and you realise he has been carrying it too. It is not a villain’s ending or a victim’s. It is two decent people who grew into different shapes, and who are tired of pretending they didn’t.

r1_x1.text: It starts as care. “Where were you?” “Who was that?” He asks lightly, with a smile, three times this week. Each question is small. Together they are starting to look like a pattern.

choices.recap: told themselves it was love
choices.label: Tell yourself it is just how he shows love

choices.recap: shared their location
choices.label: Share your location so he stops asking

choices.recap: told him it bothered them
choices.label: Tell him it bothers you
